You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 0c630a66bf10991b0ef13d27c93d7545e692ef5b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pan Bian <bianpan2016@163.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2021 20:44:23 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] net: systemport: free dev before on error path

On the error path, it should goto the error handling label to free
allocated memory rather than directly return.

Fixes: 31bc72d97656 ("net: systemport: fetch and use clock resources")
Signed-off-by: Pan Bian <bianpan2016@163.com>
Acked-by: Florian Fainelli <f.fainelli@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210120044423.1704-1-bianpan2016@163.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
---
 drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/bcmsysport.c | 6 ++++--
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/bcmsysport.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/bcmsysport.c
index b1ae9eb8f247..0404aafd5ce5 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/bcmsysport.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/bcmsysport.c
@@ -2503,8 +2503,10 @@ static int bcm_sysport_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 	priv = netdev_priv(dev);
 
 	priv->clk = devm_clk_get_optional(&pdev->dev, "sw_sysport");
-	if (IS_ERR(priv->clk))
-		return PTR_ERR(priv->clk);
+	if (IS_ERR(priv->clk)) {
+		ret = PTR_ERR(priv->clk);
+		goto err_free_netdev;
+	}
 
 	/* Allocate number of TX rings */
 	priv->tx_rings = devm_kcalloc(&pdev->dev, txq,
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a failure to properly handle memory deallocation in the error path of the `bcm_sysport_probe` function. When the clock resource allocation failed (indicated by `IS_ERR(priv->clk)`), the function was returning an error code directly without freeing the previously allocated network device memory (`dev`). This could lead to a memory leak, as the allocated memory would not be released if the function exited prematurely due to an error. The patch corrects this by introducing an error handling label (`goto err_free_netdev`) to ensure that allocated resources are freed before returning an error.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.

    Code statements:
    <text1>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a failure to properly handle memory deallocation in the error path of the `bcm_sysport_probe` function. When the clock resource allocation failed (indicated by `IS_ERR(priv->clk)`), the function was returning an error code directly without freeing the previously allocated network device memory (`dev`). This could lead to a memory leak, as the allocated memory would not be released if the function exited prematurely due to an error. The patch corrects this by introducing an error handling label (`goto err_free_netdev`) to ensure that allocated resources are freed before returning an error.
